To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) fish consumption is associated with reduced risk for cardiovascular disease; (ii) fish consumption is not associated with an increase in cardiovascular disease risk in the general U.S. adult population; (iii) fish consumption is a major source of mercury exposure in U.S. adults; and (iv) the balance between the beneficial and adverse effects of fish intake is unclear.
